current.title: Most Major Pro Sports Teams (NBA + NFL + MLB + NHL)
current.prompt: Rank the US states by combined number of franchises across the four major pro leagues (NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL).
current.disclaimer: Counts include only US-based franchises. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: California hosts LA Lakers, LA Clippers, GS Warriors, Sacramento Kings, LA Rams, LA Chargers, SF 49ers, LA Dodgers, SF Giants, LA/Anaheim Angels, Oakland A's (before Vegas move), Anaheim Ducks, LA Kings, SJ Sharks. New York includes both NY-metro NBA/NHL/NFL/MLB teams (Knicks, Nets, Rangers, Islanders, Sabres, Giants, Jets, Bills, Yankees, Mets).

findings.detail: WA is listed at rank 22 with '1 team' but Washington has Seahawks (NFL), Mariners (MLB), and Kraken (NHL) — at least 3 teams.

current.title: Most Museums (IMLS)
current.prompt: Rank the US states by total number of museums recorded in the Institute of Museum and Library Services Museum Data File.
current.disclaimer: IMLS counts include art museums, historical societies, historic sites, arboreta, zoos, aquariums, science and children's museums. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: California and Texas lead by scale; New York and Pennsylvania lead by density of historic sites.

findings.detail: Nearly every rank below the top 10 uses suspiciously round numbers (e.g. 700, 620, 600, 580, 560, 540, 500, 490, 480, 470, 450, 430, 410, 400) suggesting fabricated/estimated counts rather than actual IMLS MDF values.

current.title: Most Nobel Laureates by State of Birth (US-born winners)
current.prompt: Rank the US states by number of Nobel laureates who were born there (all Nobel categories, all-time).
current.disclaimer: Counts US-born laureates only (not naturalized or foreign-born winners affiliated with US institutions). Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: New York leads by a wide margin because of high early-20th-century immigration density; California, Illinois, Massachusetts, and Pennsylvania follow.

findings.detail: Every non-zero value uses the '~N laureates' approximate/bucket format (e.g. '~85', '~30'), which prevents precise ranking verification.

current.title: Most Public Library Systems (IMLS)
current.prompt: Rank the US states by number of public library administrative entities (systems) reported to IMLS.
current.disclaimer: Counts library administrative entities (systems), not branch locations. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: New York and Illinois have unusually high system counts because of decentralized local library districts; larger states like Texas and California have fewer systems but many branches per system.

findings.detail: Hawaii is listed at rank 50 with '1 system' — accurate (statewide system) — but Maryland at rank 48 with '20 systems' understates Maryland's 24 public library systems per IMLS 2021 PLS; values below rank 30 look rounded/approximated rather than reported.

current.title: Highest Corn Production
current.prompt: Rank US states by total corn (grain) production.
current.disclaimer: Corn for grain only (excludes silage); measured in bushels. DC not included (topic is state-scoped).
current.trivia: The Corn Belt's top two producers together grow nearly a third of all US corn.

findings.detail: Uses inconsistent decimal precision under a single 'B bushels' unit: r1-r10 shown at 2 decimals (2.55B, 0.85B), but r20+ shifts to 3 decimals (0.075B, 0.068B). Small states could be shown in millions for clarity. Precision mixing makes many rows appear tied when likely they aren't.

current.title: Highest Cost of Living
current.prompt: Rank US states (and DC) by highest overall cost-of-living index.
current.disclaimer: Composite index (US average = 100); combines grocery, housing, utilities, transport, health, and misc. DC not included (source omits it).
current.trivia: Housing is the biggest single driver — Hawaii's housing sub-index is more than triple the national average.

findings.detail: Prompt says 'Rank US states (and DC)' but disclaimer says 'DC not included (source omits it)'. Contradictory. Answer list is 50 items (no DC). Prompt should be revised.

current.title: Highest Violent Crime Rate
current.prompt: Rank US states (and DC) by highest violent crime rate per 100,000 residents.
current.disclaimer: Violent crime = murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault. Per 100,000 population. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: DC's rate is skewed by being a single dense city; among states, three of the top five are in the Deep South.

findings.detail: Disclaimer says 'FBI UCR / Crime Data Explorer, 2022' but multiple state values here differ from FBI-published 2022 figures. Furthermore, FBI's 2022 data had well-known state participation issues (transition to NIBRS meant many agencies did not report). Should note that caveat, or the ranking may reflect coverage gaps rather than crime.

current.title: Largest Federal Workforce per Capita
current.prompt: Rank US states (and DC) by federal civilian employees per 10,000 residents.
current.disclaimer: Federal civilian executive-branch employees per 10,000 residents; excludes military and postal service. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: DC's rate is more than seven times the national average; Maryland and Virginia benefit from Beltway agency HQs.

findings.detail: Values decrease by exactly 1 for ranks 15-51 (66, 64, 62, 60, 58, 56, 54, 52, 50, 49, 47, 46, 45, 44, 43, 42, 41 ... 21). This monotonic decrement pattern strongly suggests the values are synthesized/interpolated rather than pulled from FedScope. Real per-10K rates would not step down by 1 uniformly across ~40 states.

current.title: Largest Wine Production
current.prompt: Rank US states by total wine production (excluding California, which alone produces over 80% of US wine).
current.disclaimer: California is deliberately excluded to make the ranking competitive; measured in gallons produced. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: New York, Washington, and Oregon together account for over 90% of non-California US wine.

findings.detail: Prompt says 'excluding California' but disclaimer says 'Includes Washington DC'. DC has no commercial wine production of scale; the '0.001M gallons' figure at r50 for DC is not credible from Wine Institute. Also excluding CA leaves 50 items but the source (Wine Institute) does report CA — the exclusion is editorial, worth calling out in prompt more clearly.
